A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core initialization rule and retained experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments across several modalities, optimization analyses, and neural-dataset construction and classification results in Tables 1 and 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline evaluations, sensitivity analyses, novel-view synthesis experiments and wave-equation reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The initialization rule in Eq. (3), including leaving output-layer weights unscaled, remains unchanged. The new NeRF application introduces a limited adaptation: WS applies only to the volume-density network, leaving the color network outside the scaling procedure (Appendix F.6).

E1.justification: v2 adds novel-view synthesis on NeRF-synthetic Lego and Drums, plus Gaussian-pulse wave-equation reconstruction and temporal extrapolation from initial observations (Appendices F.6–F.7). The original image, occupancy, spherical, audio and neural-dataset tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from seven to nine baselines by adding MFN and Sinc NF across the original domains. These methods also enter the qualitative comparisons, while Xavier panels disappear from the image, audio and spherical examples despite its retained quantitative row. MFN additionally enters the replacement long-training comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include two NeRF resolutions with 300/600-epoch budgets, a 40,000-step PDE experiment, and batch-size and learning-rate sweeps. The earlier longer-training comparison is replaced by a scheduled 5,000-step Kodak study. The stated spherical-data learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 1e-5; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained spectral, gradient-decoupling and conditioning analyses, v2 adds Hessian eigenspectrum snapshots, mini-batch sensitivity, scaling tests with other activations, and learning-rate dependence of the optimal scale (Figures 11 and 13–15). The earlier multi-domain continuation analysis is replaced by substantially longer Kodak train/test curves in Figure 23.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting for the principal data-fitting experiments. Added Table 1 baseline rows follow this practice. No changed run count, new confidence-interval procedure or significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 entries and Table 3 remain unchanged, but v2 adds baseline scores, diagnostic curves and new task outcomes. Examples include 28.17 dB for WS on 800×800 Lego after 300 epochs and initial-time PDE MSE of 2.8e-5. v1's longer-budget Table 4 is removed; the replacement Kodak study reports peak test PSNR of 37.45 dB under its different training protocol.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.3 develops a two-layer eNTK decomposition and conditional Gaussian-kernel/eigenvalue arguments relating scaling to conditioning (Eqs. 52–56), incorporating an explicitly attributed theorem. Appendix B.1 also restores omitted W^(3) factors in Eqs. (31)–(32). The original distribution-preservation and harmonic results otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims: up to 10× faster SNF training, preserved generalization at moderate scaling, richer high-frequency representations and better conditioning. The added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their central novelty.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the previously open question about other architectures with specific applicability boundaries: GaussNet and Sinc NF can fit faster while generalization worsens, and WIRE can deteriorate. It adds interpretations concerning Hessian outliers, learning-rate-dependent scale selection and extended-training generalization. The PDE discussion acknowledges unavailable ground truth beyond the initial time.

D1.justification: New Appendices F.1–F.3 disclose tuning grids and layerwise learning-rate compensation for existing analyses. Further additions document baseline settings, NeRF network sizes and codebase, and scheduled long-training learning rates. Conversely, v1's reproducibility statement promising public code is removed without replacement project-code access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of sinusoidal activations beyond neural fields, including generative models, low-rank learning and compression. The new kernel and Hessian analyses substantially expand connections to Gaussian kernels, spectral conditioning and periodically activated networks. MFN and Sinc NF also broaden the comparison-related literature; the central training-efficiency positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. Changes include targeted related-work and conclusion rewrites, publication-header and affiliation updates, acknowledgments, theorem renumbering, and reorganized appendices. Most expansion consists of new scientific material rather than extensive rewriting of retained content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces target-PSNR training-step bars with multi-method learning curves. Table 1 gains baseline rows, qualitative grids are rearranged, and new Hessian, sensitivity, NeRF and PDE displays are added. The earlier long-training table disappears, while a NeRF table and extended train/test plots provide different comparisons.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central speed/generalization claim through additional baselines, mini-batch and learning-rate tests, training-to-saturation curves and held-out-view evaluation. Newly disclosed tuning procedures also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of the earlier multi-domain long-training table and code-release promise. The new theoretical argument remains conditional, and PDE extrapolation lacks later-time ground-truth validation, so those additions provide more limited support.
